Reporting from Amsterdam
Posted November 26, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored Advanced Nutrients.

Two Canadian seed companies walked away with the top prizes for bud.

Having BC breeders beat them in their hometown was an indication of a decline in the Dutch dominance in cannabis breeding as the local growers face harassment from a prohibitionist government. Some of my friends here are even talking moving to Spain, where things seem to be going rapidly in the right direction. Indeed, there is more pessimism in the Dutch cannabis community than I have seen in years.
From 1999, see
 The Dutch Outlaw Growing Marijuana Seeds, But Not Selling Them -- Analysis By Richard Cowan

The problem is that the small-town prohibitionists of the Christian Democratic Party dominate the current coalition government. However, there are many instances in Dutch history in which Amsterdam has had to stand its ground and insist that tolerance is good for business.

Consequently, my more political sources are quite certain that the coffee shop system itself is not in danger. As incomprehensible as it may seem to Americans and even Canadians, the Dutch police, prosecutors and judges are some of the staunchest supporters of the system, especially in Amsterdam.
See
 Dutch Government Reconfirms Coffee Shop Policy. Drops Any Mention of Closing Border Shops. The Justice Minister Is Educating the Prime Minister.

Next week MarijuanaNews will have a much longer report on the Dutch situation.
